title: How loud the old trumpeters played
summary: Punch says Armstrong called him one of the loudest in New Orleans, compared with Keppard's strength low down.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: What about the volume on the different trumpet players? How loud did they play?

Well, the loudest one you mean honey? Mm-hmm. Well, I don't know, but the teppan they used to yell me at, Ramport and Julian, I played at National Park, that's there in Willow. I don't know how loud I was playing, but they said they could yell me at night. So Louis Armstrong himself told me I was about as loud a fella that had in New Orleans, 10 times. Loud, strong, you know.
Were you as loud as Geppin?
Well, not down there where he was, you know. But I mean, I was loud all the way up, but he down that staff, that low-seeing thing, man, tightest wall over there.
You cut through. Yeah. But you were playing high. Yeah, that's right. If he'd been playing high.
He sure was he was not hard, boy.
If he'd been playing high, he'd probably knocked over Stradillie.
